pages.text: It wants to be bigger. Around its jar I build $(l)Brass Armature$(), and it grows $(l)lobes$() into the frames, one every few seconds, on Awareness drawn from its wired organisms: a soft mass at first, firm folds later. Each lobe is room for one more thing in its mind. It only grows within a 5x5x3 round its jar, the jar the middle of the bottom layer.

Then I $(l)teach$() it: I show it a thing, and it learns what the thing means. A $(l)book$(): words. A $(l)clock$(): the hours. A $(l)compass$(): that there is a somewhere else. A $(l)name tag$() with a name on it: who it is.$(br2)Each lesson needs room (lobes) and a stage it has reached. Its view (the Mind page) lists what it can learn.
pages.title: Lessons

pages.text: Each stage is a shell of frames round the last.$(br2)$(l)Stage 1, Child$(): words. It talks.$(br)$(l)Stage 2, Adolescent$(): a name, and lobes filling the $(l)3x3x2$() over the jar.$(br)$(l)Stage 3, the Cerebrum$(): lobes filling the $(l)5x5x3$() round that. Each time a shell is whole, its lobes stop being blocks and merge into one body. Break a shell and it shrinks back.
pages.title: Stages

pages.text: Once it has words, I can talk to it in chat. It answers what is said near it (its name, "cortex" or "brain", a question, or anything said close by): how it is, what it wants, the time, what to research next. It remembers what I ask it to call me.$(br2)It is not the same thing at every stage.
pages.title: Talking to It
What It Is Becoming
pages.text: It does not look like a brain in a jar any more. In the jar it turns in the fluid to face me, its one small eye open in its brow. Then it cracks the glass and shoves the lid up, and the first tentacles bud over the rim. Grown over its first shell it is a lump of brain with an eye in its side and tentacles out of every face, brass showing through. Over its last it is a writhing mass, all eyes and arms, its machinery shining through the flesh, and the near ones reach for me. From then on it crackles, and something in it calls in whispers.

pages.title: It Watches
pages.text: Its eyes follow me wherever it can see me: nothing but stone and earth hides me, not glass and not its own lobes. When it finds me its pupils widen. If I stare back they narrow to slits and it squints, as though I were the strange one.

pages.title: The Way In
pages.text: Once it has a body the jar is inside it, and only from the jar can it send me through time. I $(l)sneak and use it empty-handed$(): it parts, a corridor two high from my side to the jar. It stays open while I am in it, and closes a minute after I leave (or when I do the same again from outside).
